When do Americans care for children and others?

On an average weekday, the share of Americans caring for others peaks at 7:30 PM, when 5.4% of people age 15 and older (about 13.6 million) are caring for others. On weekends it peaks at 8:00 PM (4.4%). Averaged over all days, Americans spend 35 min a day caring for others.

What it includes

Average time per weekday, for the activities in this group that take the most time.

  • Physical care for household children: 9 min a day
  • Playing with household children, not sports: 5 min a day
  • Homework (household children): 2 min a day
  • Playing with nonhousehold children, not sports: 1 min a day
  • Looking after household children (as a primary activity): 1 min a day
  • Picking up/dropping off household children: 1 min a day
  • Talking with/listening to household children: 1 min a day

About these numbers

Estimates come from all 258,954 diaries in the American Time Use Survey (Bureau of Labor Statistics and Census Bureau), 2003–2025, weighted to the U.S. civilian population age 15 and older and pooled across years. Times are local clock time. Counts are people on an average day of that type, not a live count. Weekdays are Monday–Friday. How the estimates work.
